$comment: Vectors for the three errors[].match kinds (spec/03-manifest-dsl.md#errors) and how they interact with a step's own status_map (spec/03-manifest-dsl.md#how-errors-interacts-with-status_map): path/equals against the response body, http_status against the raw HTTP status regardless of body content, and transport against an absent response entirely. errors is always evaluated before status_map; a match short-circuits the step's own emit/state entirely.

cases.description: http_status match fires purely on status code, independent of what the body says

body.message: some provider-specific text that mentions nothing about auth

cases.description: a second http_status entry matches its own distinct code
path/equals match fires on body content with a 200 status, the common case for a provider that reports failure in-band rather than via HTTP status
http_status 200 with a body that matches no path/equals entry and isn't one of the declared http_status codes falls through to this step's own status_map, not to any errors entry
cases.note: Falls through to status_map: success -> whatever step that value is mapped to.

cases.description: transport match fires when no response was received at all, independent of any http_status or body (there is neither)
a matched errors entry bypasses this step's own status_map entirely, even when the body would also satisfy status_map.values for some key
cases.why: errors is checked before status_map (spec/03-manifest-dsl.md#how-errors-interacts-with-status_map); a matched errors entry means status_map is never consulted for this response, regardless of what value would otherwise have matched there.

cases.description: http_status alone, without any path/equals entry present, still resolves correctly when only one errors entry could apply
cases.note: A transport-level absence of a body (as opposed to an empty JSON object) never prevents an http_status match, since http_status never inspects the body at all.
